quote: decrees of the senate were not to be passed in consequence of rumours fabricated by private persons for the gratification of magistrates
notes: Senate elders refuse Flaminius a city legion raised on privately circulated rumours, voting instead for tumultuary levies outside Italy (livy:en:35:2).

quote: rather than Quintus Minucius should be called away from a war, in which no progress had been made, to suffer an interregnum
notes: Senate threatens to let an interregnum occur unless consul Cornelius returns to hold the elections, and he yields (livy:en:35:6).

quote: a fraudulent course had been adopted —that of transferring the securities to subjects of some of the allied states
notes: Creditors evade Roman interest laws by channelling loans through allied citizens, overwhelming debtors with unlimited usury until the senate orders registration of such loans (livy:en:35:7).

quote: Marcus Sempronius, plebeian tribune, by direction of the senate, proposed to the people, and the people ordered
notes: Tribune Marcus Sempronius carries a law making loans between Romans and allies subject to the same usury rules as between citizens, closing the loophole (livy:en:35:7).

quote: the plebeian tribunes, Marcus and Caius Titinius, declared, that they would enter their protest, if the senate passed any decree on the subject
notes: Metellus blocks consul Merula's demand for a thanksgiving and triumph over the Boii, citing Marcellus's contradictory letters, and the tribunes Titinii threaten their protest (livy:en:35:8).

quote: a Latin colony was established in the Thurian territory by commissioners appointed for the purpose
notes: Commissioners settle a Latin colony of 3,000 foot and 300 horse in the Thurian territory, reserving a third of the land for future colonists (livy:en:35:9).

quote: with regard to the election of consuls, emulation was more fiercely kindled than was ever known before
notes: The fiercest consular canvass yet seen pits the brothers of Flamininus and Africanus against each other; Quinctius wins and Africanus fails even to carry Laelius (livy:en:35:10).

quote: They prosecuted to conviction many of the farmers of the public pastures
notes: The aediles Lepidus and Paulus convict many graziers of the public pastures and spend the fines on gilded shields and porticoes (livy:en:35:10).

quote: ambassadors should be sent to each of the kings; not only to sound their dispositions
notes: At the Naupactum assembly the Aetolian praetor Thoas carries a motion to send envoys to Nabis, Philip and Antiochus to stir them to war with Rome (livy:en:35:12).

quote: others, who more firmly adhered to the alliance with Rome, he put to death
notes: Nabis's emissaries sow dissension in the Laconian coastal towns, bribing some leading men and killing those loyal to the Roman alliance (livy:en:35:13).

quote: his father, thinking that his heir trod too closely on the heels of his own old age, had him taken off by poison
notes: Seleucid, not Roman: the death of Antiochus's heir is popularly blamed on the king himself as a dynastic poisoning by eunuchs (livy:en:35:15).

quote: There was, this year also, a warm competition, three patricians suing for one place
notes: With war looming the senate recalls the consul for early elections; after a warm three-way patrician contest Scipio, rejected the year before, is returned (livy:en:35:24).

quote: they summoned a council at Sicyon, and also sent deputies to Titus Quinctius to ask his advice
notes: The Achaean council at Sicyon, after consulting Rome and Quinctius, unanimously votes war on Nabis, leaving its conduct to the praetor Philopoemen (livy:en:35:25).

quote: Eurylochus, a deputy of the Magnetians, and others of that faction, wished for a total change of measures
notes: At the Magnetian council in Demetrias the Magnetarch Eurylochus's faction, fearing the city's return to Philip, courts Antiochus and the Aetolians; the clash drives him into exile (livy:en:35:31, flight in 35:32).

quote: a decree was passed that Antiochus should be invited to vindicate the liberty of Greece
notes: With Quinctius still present, the Aetolian council decrees that Antiochus be invited to free Greece and arbitrate between Aetolia and Rome (livy:en:35:33).

quote: making themselves masters of Demetrias, Chalcis, and Lacedaemon
notes: The Aetolian Apocleti secretly scheme to seize Demetrias, Chalcis and Lacedaemon, despatching Diocles, Thoas and Alexamenus respectively (livy:en:35:34).

quote: parties were sent to the houses of persons of the opposite faction, to put them to death
notes: Diocles's cavalry restores the exile Eurylochus and murders the opposing faction, delivering Demetrias into Aetolian hands (livy:en:35:34).

quote: their points at length penetrated his body, so that, before relief could be sent from the centre, he expired
notes: Alexamenus and the Aetolian horsemen Nabis had invited as allies cut the tyrant down during a review outside Sparta (livy:en:35:35).

quote: him they mounted on a horse, and taking arms, slew all the Aetolians whom they met straggling through the city
notes: The Spartans rally around the boy Laconicus, massacre the plundering Aetolians and kill Alexamenus, after which Philopoemen attaches Lacedaemon to the Achaean League (livy:en:35:36).

quote: he had engaged a party, composed of Euthymidas's faction, to betray the city into his hands
notes: Thoas's plan to have the exiled Euthymidas's partisans betray Chalcis miscarries when the magistrates learn of it and summon Eretrian and Carystian aid (livy:en:35:37, foiled in 35:38).

quote: In this year a colony was settled at Vibo, in pursuance of a decree of the senate and an order of the people
notes: A citizen colony of 3,700 foot and 300 horse is planted at Vibo on former Bruttian land, with fifteen acres per footman (livy:en:35:40).

quote: Many severe sentences were passed this year on usurers, who were prosecuted, as private persons, by the curule aediles
notes: The curule aediles Tuccius and Brutus win severe sentences against usurers and dedicate gilded chariots and bucklers on the Capitol from the fines (livy:en:35:41).

quote: the council voted, that the title of general should be conferred on the king
notes: After Thoas defeats Phaeneas's plea to use Antiochus as mediator rather than war-leader, the Aetolian council names the king their general with a council of thirty (livy:en:35:45).

quote: Apollodorus, the principal adviser of a revolt, being publicly charged therewith by one Leon, was condemned and driven into exile
notes: With Athens near civil war over largess-fed agitation for Antiochus, Apollodorus is condemned and exiled on Leon's charge after Quinctius intervenes (livy:en:35:50).

quote: Those who adhered to the Roman interest, on the approach of the king, withdrew from the city
notes: Under Antiochus's threats Chalcis opens its gates despite Mictio and Xenoclides, the pro-Roman party withdraws, and all Euboea submits to the king (livy:en:35:51).
